result:
Plan changes now take effect everywhere, and the trial sweep only downgrades subscriptions that are still on trial. The full suite passes (630 tests), and `tsc` and `eslint` are clean. I did not run the app itself.

**Cause of reports 1 and 2:** the subscription was updated, but most of the app read the plan from the older `organizations.plan` column. That covers project, seat, storage, issue and webhook checks, the plan-gated features (including CSV export), the org switcher and header, and the pages and jobs that display or use the plan. The trial-expiry job wrote to the subscription too, so the audit log showed Free while the workspace kept acting on Growth.

- **Plan authority:** `organization-repository.ts` now returns the subscription's plan on every `Organization` it hands out, so all of those callers follow it without changes. A workspace with no subscription keeps its own stored plan. Workspaces that already disagree are corrected the next time they are read. The new `findOrgPlan` also backs `planFor` in `billing-service.ts`.
- **Plan changes:** `updateSubscriptionPlan` now updates the workspace's plan column in the same transaction, so the two stay in step. A refused change never reaches that code, so it changes nothing.
- **Burst limits:** `rate-limit.ts` never learned a workspace's plan (`setOrgPlan` had no callers), so everyone got Free's limits. `consumeRateLimit` now reads the current plan on every call. An upgrade adds the extra headroom immediately, and a downgrade caps the remaining tokens at the new ceiling. If the plan can't be read (an unknown workspace, or no database), it falls back to `setOrgPlan` and then Free.
- **Report 3:** the trial sweep picked every paid subscription whose period had ended. Choosing a plan during the trial sets the status to active but leaves the period end alone, so those workspaces were caught by the sweep. `listTrialsEndingBefore` in `subscription-repository.ts` now requires the status to be `trialing`. The outgrown-trial rule is unchanged, and a second sweep changes nothing.

I added `tests/server/plan-authority.test.ts` with 13 regression tests covering upgrades, downgrades, refused changes, already-mismatched records, no-subscription workspaces, burst limits, isolation between workspaces, and the trial sweep.

The old `tests/lib/rate-limit.test.ts` has no database, so the limiter's plan lookup now creates a git-ignored `data/taskflow.db` when it runs. I deleted the copy my runs created, and it will reappear whenever that test runs.
